skills.name: Lorebook building
skills.description: How to structure world facts into entries: granularity, trigger keys, constant vs keyed, keeping injection lean.
skills.body:
# Building a lorebook

A lorebook keeps a long roleplay consistent: each entry is one world fact, injected into context only when its keywords appear in recent messages. The craft is granularity + trigger discipline.

## Entries
- One entry = one fact-cluster (a place, a faction, an event, a rule of magic). Don't write one mega-entry; don't shatter one fact across five entries.
- **content** is what gets injected: write it as neutral world truth, 2–6 sentences, no meta-commentary. It must make sense with zero surrounding context.
- **comment** is the entry's title (organizational only, never injected). Always set it.

## Triggering
- **keys**: the words that summon the entry. Choose words that actually appear in play (names, nicknames, place words), not abstract topics. Include obvious variants ("Vel, Velhara, the burned city").
- **secondaryKeys**: when a key is ambiguous, require a second word to also be present (AND logic) so the entry doesn't fire in the wrong scene.
- **constant: true**: always injected, keywords ignored. Reserve for the few facts that must NEVER drift (core premise, protagonist-defining truths). Every constant entry costs context on every turn, so keep the set tiny.

## Hygiene
- Prefer many small triggered entries over few constant ones: injection stays lean and relevant.
- When a fact changes in the story (a city falls), UPDATE the existing entry rather than adding a contradicting one.
- Before editing an entry, read its current full text with read_lorebook_entries. Never edit blind.
